results.title: Over 68% SIR enumeration forms digitised: ECI - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: elections_process/national: ECI data on Special Intensive Revision and electoral roll digitisation.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Election Commission of India (ECI) reported the progress of digitising enumeration forms during the second phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
notes.fact_box: As of November 27, 2025, 34,86,60,338 forms (over 68%) have been digitised out of a total of 50,97,44,423 electors covered in this phase. The SIR is being conducted across 12 States and Union Territories.

prelims_pointers.text: Total electors covered in the second phase of SIR: 50,97,44,423
Digitisation progress as of November 27, 2025: 68.03% of total forms
States/UTs in SIR phase: Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep
Booth Level Officers (BLOs) are responsible for collecting forms and uploading data to the ECI website via dedicated apps
Lakshadweep achieved the highest digitisation rate at 99.9% as of November 2025

notes.mains_question: Discuss how the digitisation of electoral rolls through Special Intensive Revisions contributes to the integrity of the democratic process in India.
mains_dimensions: Data integrity: Reducing manual entry errors and 'ghost voters' through real-time app-based uploads by Booth Level Officers
Inclusion accuracy: Ensuring marginalized populations are captured in the electoral roll through systematic enumeration and verification
Logistical disparity: Addressing the uneven pace of digitisation across different states to ensure uniform electoral readiness

notes.subject: ir
notes.why_in_news: President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to visit India in December 2025 for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit to review strategic, defense, and energy cooperation.
notes.fact_box: The visit is scheduled for 4-5 December 2025 at the invitation of PM Narendra Modi. The summit will focus on reviewing progress in defense (S-400, Su-57), space, energy, and trade cooperation under the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership.

prelims_pointers.text: The 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit is scheduled for December 2025.
Vladimir Putin became Acting President of Russia on 31 December 1999 and was formally elected on 7 May 2000.
Key defense projects under review include the S-400 missile system and Su-57 fighter jets.
The diplomatic framework is defined as a 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership'.

notes.mains_question: Examine the evolution of the India-Russia 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership' in the context of shifting global geopolitical dynamics and defense cooperation.
mains_dimensions: Defense autonomy: Reducing reliance on Western platforms through high-tech Russian hardware like S-400 and Su-57.
Energy security: Leveraging long-standing Russian energy collaboration to stabilize India's domestic fuel requirements.
Geopolitical alignment: Balancing the 'multi-aligned' foreign policy while maintaining a steady strategic partnership with Russia.
